title: Alexanderplatz History - FAQ
subtitle: Where the name comes from, what was lost and what you can still see.

items.a: The square was renamed in **1805** after **Tsar Alexander I** of Russia visited Prussia. Before that it was the **Ochsenmarkt**, a cattle market and parade ground outside the city gate.

items.q: What happened to the Berolina statue?
items.a: The copper Berolina by Emil Hundrieser stood on the square from **1895**. She was removed in 1927 for the U-Bahn works, returned in 1933 and was **dismantled during the war**, in 1942 according to most sources, and probably melted down. A small model survives in the Märkisches Museum.

items.q: What are the oldest buildings on Alexanderplatz?
items.a: Apart from the 1882 railway viaduct, the oldest buildings are the **Alexanderhaus** and the **Berolinahaus** by Peter Behrens, built between **1929 and 1932**. Both are listed monuments.

items.q: When was Alexanderplatz rebuilt by the GDR?
items.a: After a competition in **1964**. The Haus des Lehrers was finished in 1964, the **TV Tower** and the **World Clock** in 1969, and the fountain, the hotel and the department store around **1970**.

items.q: What happened on Alexanderplatz on 4 November 1989?
items.a: East Berliners held a huge demonstration for free speech and free elections. Estimates run from **500,000 to nearly a million** people. The Wall opened **five days later**.

items.q: How long do I need to see the history of Alexanderplatz?
items.a: About **30 minutes**. Start at the World Clock, look at the Behrens buildings by the station, walk to the fountain and the **Haus des Lehrers** mural, and finish under the TV Tower.
